title: UCC § 2-207 — formation and unmatched terms
summary: UCC § 2-207 separates whether parties have formed a sales contract from which terms enter that contract when their communications do not match.
notes:
Subsection (1) addresses an expression of acceptance or written confirmation, including the exception for acceptance expressly conditioned on assent to new terms. Subsection (2) addresses additional terms and contains special rules for transactions between merchants. Subsection (3) recognizes a contract through both parties’ conduct when their writings do not establish one, and determines its terms from agreement and applicable supplementary law. Dorton, C. Itoh, Bayway, and Northrop examine different parts of this structure. Hill and Klocek disagree about its application to later-delivered consumer terms. Follow the relevant route before deciding which party’s clause controls.

Subsection (1) recognizes a definite and seasonable expression of acceptance or timely confirmation despite additional or different terms, subject to its expressly conditional proviso. Subsection (2) treats additions as proposals and supplies the between-merchants rule and its exceptions. Subsection (3) addresses conduct recognizing a contract despite insufficient writings and provides agreed terms plus supplementary Code terms. The chapter gives extensive quotations and applications, but the complete SEL text and comments should still be kept as a separate assigned source. Northrop’s dispute about different terms and Hill’s one-form argument must be recorded as disagreements, rather than smoothed into one rule.
